metadata.title: Claude, Matter Workspace.
metadata.subtitle: One Matter at a Time
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Teardown register: does Claude's matter-workspace skill blend every matter into one shared pool, or keep this matter separate? Lands the carry-out that a skill stays inside the matter it's pointed at by default, and only reads across matters once the practice turns that on in CLAUDE.md.
metadata.anchor_pair: B03 -> B06 (matter-workspace's single SKILL.md: planted, then returned to)
metadata.one_flag: N/A - no inference beat; every claim is generic, verifiable skill mechanics plus the source's own stated design tell (cross-matter isolation)

beats.narration_text: Natural read: Claude picks up matter-workspace and already knows every matter you have, all pooled. Wrong branch — by default it stays inside just this one. Here's when that changes.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Claude already knows every matter I have.', hesitates on 'every', corrects to 'just this one', lands the real question

props.text:
Claude already knows
every matter I have.
Is that right?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('every' -> 'just this one') is visible on a late frame. NOTE (fix, 2026-08-30): the component's triggerWords match SINGLE TOKENS only (whitespace-split, punctuation-stripped) -- a two-word trigger like 'every matter' can never match a token and silently never fires. Trigger must be exactly one word; the replacement may be multi-word.

beats.narration_text: Hear "Claude has a matter-workspace skill" and the machinery you picture is one shared pool — every case you've ever discussed, blended, ready for Claude to draw from anytime. That's what the name suggests is happening under the hood.

Here's what's actually happening: open a brand-new matter, ask Claude about specifics from a different case, and it comes back with nothing to draw on. By default, matter-workspace walls every matter off from every other one. They optimized for isolation at the expense of any cross-case recall.

production_viz.label: NOTHING TO DRAW ON
production_viz.caption: there was nothing to draw on

beats.narration_text: Take it apart: a skill is one file. matter-workspace is a folder holding a single SKILL.md — plain-language instructions Claude reads before it touches a matter. No compiled logic, no hidden layer running underneath. The file is the program — a deliberate choice to keep the routine readable and auditable instead of clever.

The mechanism: Claude reads that file's Steps section and executes it top to bottom. Linear. No branching unless a step itself says to branch. Straight execution between the words on the page and what actually runs — no interpretation layer to guess about.

Here's the constraint that reveals the priority: by default, matter-workspace never reads across matters. It only draws on another case once cross-matter context is switched on in the practice's CLAUDE.md. They optimized for isolation at the expense of frictionless recall — and put the switch in one specific file so the choice is explicit, never silent.

production_viz.label: ISOLATED BY DEFAULT
production_viz.caption: the switch lives in the practice file

beats.narration_text: So matter-workspace was never handing Claude one shared pool across every case. What it actually guarantees: every time it runs, Claude reads that same SKILL.md and stays inside the matter it's pointed at — unless the CLAUDE.md switch is on. Isolation-by-default is the whole design.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — SAME FILE, SAME MATTER

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — SAME FILE, SAME MATTER
production_viz.caption: same file, same matter, every run

beats.narration_text: Neither observation is proof of the state. Watching Claude answer correctly inside one matter doesn't prove it's blind to every other one — cross-matter context might already be switched on. And Claude missing a detail from another matter doesn't prove isolation is working — it might simply not have been asked. Behavior can't tell you which side of the switch you're on; only the CLAUDE.md file can.
A matter-workspace skill doesn't blend your cases into one pool — by default it stays inside the matter it's pointed at, and it only reads across matters once the practice turns that on in CLAUDE.md.
